## Types of Roles

- Many - math graduates who can write code are popular - high endurance, abstraction, creative thinking:
- Data: Analyst / Engineer / Scientist / Architect
- ML: Scientist / Engineer / Consultant
- Statistician
- Bioinformatics, Biostatistics, Cheminformatics
- Computational Marketing
- Quantitative Analyst
- Software: Developer / Engineer / Architect
- Risk Analyst
- Operations Research Analyst
- Actuary
- Teacher, Professor

## Typical Day

- Meetings
- Triaging requests on Slack
- Reading research papers (specific positions)
- Writing code
- Sourcing data
- Daily stand up (ritual: team progress, plans, updates & blockers)
- Training
- Presentations
- Demo days

## Work Cultures

- Reflective
- High Pressure
- High Performance
- Competitive, Collaborative
- Slow, Fast
- Impacting
- Toxic
- Break Things, Move Fast
- Meaningful
- Innovation, Staid

## Devices

- Laptop
- Data & communications locked to device, everything monitored
- Traditional: business laptop with windows
- Creatives: usually provide Mac/Linux
- Take to every meeting
- Don’t open whatsapp/fb/instagram/personal email or install programs
- Personal Phone (BYOD)
- Install monitoring software
- Access work docs/email/comms
- Cloud
- Some legacy organizations have servers
- Organizations processing big data use cloud:
    - Amazon AWS, Google GCP, Microsoft Azure, Huawei, Alibaba Cloud
- Tech & start-ups are mostly using cloud

## Communications

- Everything will be locked down and visible
- Use email/chat only for work
- DM service like Slack/Discord/Teams
- Reply quickly and professionally
- Keep communications short and business-like, not too formal
- Email is mostly for old economy companies
- Use calendar; be punctual

## Data

- Small Data
- Shared drive: KB, MB, GB data volume
- Working on laptops
- Legacy industry applications
- Some working in Excel
- xslx, tsv, csv, txt, db, sql file formats
- Big Data
- Cloud based storage: GB, PB, XB, YB data volume
- Work with servers using Python, SQL (sometimes R, Node, Java)
- Expect security to be paramount PII (Super sensitive data)
- avro, parquet, orc, json, bson, fasta, fastq, sql file formats

## Compensation

- Salary
- Stock
- Vacations
- Perks: Massages, Relocation, Healthcare, Education/Travel Budget, Work From Home, Gifts, Food

## Getting Interview Invitation

## Hiring: Organization Perspective

- Time is money
- Can cost 5-15% of the total budget, 30% of first year salary, 200% to replace a bad hire
- Productivity declines
- Too many online applications
- Filtering is error prone
- Bad hires are a weight on the organization
- Boring & exhausting process
- Serious candidates need to demonstrate motivation

## Opinions

- Learn to work in groups of 2-5 people, ideally cross functional teams
- Many organizations work on quarterly budgets and allocations
- Could apply around the quarters (Dec/Jan, March/April, June/July, Sept/Oct)
- Probably best to get to a big city, you’ll learn more quickly working with highly skilled people
- Live close to work for the first year (even if it’s a small apartment share)
- Work crazy hard for the first 6 months
- Don’t mention you want to go back to university (PhD/Masters)

## Networking

- High Probability of Interview:
- Friends
- Family
- Conferences
- LinkedIn coffee meetings with potential colleagues
- Not fair, but filtering is expensive and boring

## Candidate Qualities

- Be nice (your prospective colleagues will spend more time with you than their partner)
- Don’t be nervous or desperate
- Don’t boast
- Listen carefully, speak slowly
- Go to office if possible

## Types of Recruiters

- External (not ideal - will eat into your compensation - maybe 30%)
- Internal
- Semi-internal (contracted by business)

## LinkedIn/Indeed

- Don’t apply for jobs directly

## Job Description

- Don’t worry
- Only a guide (sometimes a senior post, will consider a good junior)
- Often copy/pasted by HR
- No one completes all the requirements
- Work out if the position is in a cost center or revenue driver for the business

## Tailored Resume

- Make the resume fit the job
- Highlight skills relevant to the jobs
- Remove skills not relevant

## Direct Approach

- Google then write to the internal recruiter
- Write to googled prospective colleagues (LinkedIn, BlueSky, X, Mastodon)

## Technical Screening: Mariel

## Invited Interview Process

## Understand the Organization

- Understand their business model
- Know sector themes
- Industry press
- CEO/CFO/CTO/Prospective Colleagues Interviews/Posts
- Understand revenue/profit/cost sources of the organization

## Your Persona

- Smile (Lots)
- Positive energy
- Confident, can do attitude
- Professionally attractive version of yourself
- Dress code depends on industry sector
    - Traditional (Law, Finance, Govt, University): Conservative dress, hide tattoos, piercings
    - Creative (Tech, Media, Arts, Startups): More permissive on self-expression

## Interviewers Team

- People Ops (HR)
    - Senior
    - Junior
- Team Members
    - Business Area Manager
    - Hiring Manager
    - Second Manager
- Random Business Areas
    - Random jr to check fit with culture
    - Random Manager to check fit with culture

## Recruitment Process

- First Stage Screening
- Second Stage Screening
- Technical Screening
- Interview Panel
- Technical Interview

## First Screen: HR Interview

- Check candidate is suitable and realistic
- Filter out completely unaware

## Follow Up Call/Email

- Very important
- Send a polite email thanking the interviewer(s) for taking the time to interview you
- Do this for after every interview - make sure to write to all interviewers
- Many can fail at this stage

## Second Screen: Small Technical Challenge

## Interview Panel

- 0.5-3 days
- On-site at the office (Could be off-site at a hotel/resort)
- 5-8 interviews with 2-3 interviewers in each interview

## Interviews: Interview Panel

- Introduce yourself, small talk about weather, journey
- If asked, mention you have other interviews in process
- Wide ranging types (group, in-tray, interaction)
- Related to job
- Show enthusiasm for the mission of the organization
- Smile lots
- It’s not an academic free thinking environment

## Psychometrics

- Personality Test
- Try to give middle response
- Usually not very important
- Aptitude Test
- Looking at repetitive baseline skills
- Could be important for specific roles
- Not good for creative positions

## Technical Coding Interview

- Can practice hundreds online (people do: [leetcode.com](http://leetcode.com), [hackerank.com](http://hackerrank.com))
- Pattern matching
- Watch YouTube for examples
- Big-O, Loops, Recursion, Conditionals
- Programming Style

## Technical Interview: Mariel

## The Rejection

## Rejection

- Slow response (days to weeks)
- Don’t take it personally
- Many reasons
    - Bad Organization Fit
    - Funding Withdrawn
    - Better Candidate
    - Internal Candidate
    - Poor performance

## Feedback

- Valuable
- Try to get specifics
- Suggestions for how to improve
- Be grateful

## The Offer

## Offer Process

- Fast Response (Hours to Days)
- Informal call/email from HR
- Subject to offer, accept provisionally if you like the organization
- Formal offer: can be a zoom with all interviewers
- Try to Negotiate

## Offer Negotiation

- 10-30% increase possible
- stock/salary/sign-on bonus/vacation/other benefits
- startup stock options mostly don’t work out
- Often the improvement is stock or relocation costs (might not be worth much)
